blend.lean: Germanic-heavy - an Anglo-Saxon warrior-aristocracy settled over a Romano-Brittonic populace and largely Anglicized it. This INVERTS the old Gundic lean (which was Celtic-backbone / Germanic-overlay).

_note: REPLACES the old Gundic kit (catalog 7 / HYB_01). Cross-family blend (Germanic + Celtic), now leaning GERMANIC: a 'Ye Olde Merry England' / Arthurian analog - Anglo-Saxon (Old English) kingdoms grown over a Romano-Brittonic substrate. Backbone = Germanic (anglo_saxon: Old English phonology, the burh-and-tun land, the cyning/ealdor/thegn register, the dithematic Aethel-/Os-/-wald name-stock); substrate = Celtic (brythonic: Caer-/Pen- toponyms, ap- patronymics, initial mutation, the lateral ll, the older Brittonic name-stock and the seintiau). Common-word lexicon and rank titles use the real Old-English and Welsh registers (allowed, catalog 5.3); DEITY names are morphs of the Agrippan canon from both parents (Anglo-Saxon reflexes primary, Brythonic variants secondary), never real gods. CIV/CLAN DECIDED (2026-06-27): Clanhold. Both parent bases - Thiodmark (Germanic) and Albawyn (Celtic) - are assigned Clanhold (gdd-culture-emergence-and-territory.md §3.2), so by the inheritance rule (Clan+Clan -> Clan) Brythald is a Clanhold culture: a Germanic clan-kingship (the cyning and his sworn hearth-troop) over a Brittonic substrate, NOT a centralized feudal state. STILL OPEN: alignment (Lawful vs Neutral) is a design choice - Arthurian Camelot reads Lawful (the just high-king and the sworn fellowship), an older Anglo-Saxon heathen layer reads Neutral. [UPDATE 2026-06-27: all human cultures allow Lawful/Neutral/Chaotic (per-hybrid alignment restriction removed). Ruler/domain DISPLAY titles are now English (or an approved foreign term); conlang titles moved to ruler_native/domain_native for NPC dialogue. Deities unchanged: canonical Agrippan pantheon via the per-family morph method.]

phonology.palette: Old English (Anglo-Saxon) backbone: root-initial stress; palatalized velars (c>ch, sc>sh, g>y; cild>child, sceap>sheep, gear>year); the dental fricatives th/dh; front rounded vowels and phonemic vowel length; ea/eo diphthongs; the guttural h (/x/, niht); the dithematic name-stock (Aethel-, Os-, Ead-, Wulf-, -wald, -here, -ric, -mund). A Brythonic substrate adds initial consonant mutation, the lateral fricative ll, Caer-/Pen-/Tre- toponyms and ap-/map- patronymics. Theophoric on the Anglo-Saxon reflexes (Thulor-, Eorland-) with Brythonic variants (Toran-, Orlann-).
phonology.phonotactics: CVC with OE clusters (st, sc, hl, hr, hw, wr, cn); root-initial stress; dithematic compounds; the Brythonic substrate adds mutation-clusters and the lateral fricative.

sound_changes: Brythonic lateral ll and lenition adapted to OE: word-initial ll>hl, medial ll>ll, soft-mutated b/d/g>p/t/c (de-lenited to the OE stop)
OE palatalization imposed on inherited roots: c>ch and sc>sh before front vowels (caer kept hard as a fixed toponym; coed>chedd)
Brythonic w/y/dd vowels and spirants folded into the OE system: w>ea/eo or u, y>i, final -dd>th, and the Brythonic -on/-en/-w endings drop
OE root-initial stress on every word; OE clusters (st, sc, hl, hr, hw) permitted; the Brythonic penult-stress is overridden
very short Brythonic roots take an OE -e or -a; OE th/dh, ea/eo diphthongs and the guttural h retained as signature phonemes
fusion_rules.source_tilt: land/water/terrain words lean Brythonic substrate roots (afon, cwm, pen, caer, nant, llyn, coed run through the OE filter); kin-line/quality/abstract/rule/war words from Old English roots (sunu, micel, eald, halig, mearc); every root then filtered to one OE-shaped phonology so the split is inaudible

lexicon._note: Single fused tongue derived via phonology.fusion_rules (gdd-hybrid-conlang-fusion.md): Brythonic land/water/terrain roots + Old English rule/kin/quality roots, all run through one OE-shaped sound-law (palatalization, lateral-ll adaptation, root-initial stress, dropped Brythonic endings); portmanteaus mark the blended institutions and bloodline. One Anglo-Brittonic tongue, not Old English with a Welsh gloss.

morphology.patronymic_form: Old English patronymic -sunu (son of) / -ing (of the kin of); the noble houses keep dithematic lineage-names and -ingas / -ingatun lineage-steads; the Brythonic substrate keeps ap- / map- (son of) and the tud (kindred/people).
morphology.compounding_rule: [quality|feature|animal](stem) + element: Sweart-weald (black-forest), Read-dun (red-hill), Aesc-burh (ash-fort); the Brythonic substrate yields Caer- and Pen- compounds (Caer-Vyrdin, Pen-bryn) and the -ingas lineage-steads.

title_ladder.government: clanhold (a Germanic clan-kingship over a Brittonic substrate: the cyning and his aethelings, the ealdormen of the shires, the thegns sworn to the hearth-troop; the witan counsels, the Brittonic tud endures beneath - kindred-and-comitatus bound, not a centralized feudal state)
title_ladder._tiers_note: Anglo-Saxon ladder, ascending, with the Bretwalda (the 'Britain-ruler', wide-overlord of all Bryten - the Arthurian high-king) at the crown. Thegn (sworn retainer-lord) barony; Mearc-weard (march-warden) march; Ealdorman (shire-ruler) county over a Scir (shire); Heretoga (war-leader; *harja-tugon) duchy; Undercyning (under-king) principality; Cyning (king) kingdom over a Cynerice; Bretwalda (over-king of Britain) empire over the Brytenrice. The witega (sage-prophet) and the Brittonic derwydd stand outside the ladder. Brythonic substrate variants at the crown: Penteyrn (chief-lord) / Gwledig (the Romano-British over-ruler, cf. the Arthurian Dux). Rank titles fuse the real Old-English and Welsh registers (allowed).
title_ladder.display_policy: Ruler/domain titles shown in setting-gen, domain lists and vassal trees are ENGLISH (or an approved commonly-known foreign term where set in 'ruler'). The *_native conlang forms are for NPC DIALOGUE ONLY, never for structural/UI displays.

people_name_convention.order: Old English dithematic personal name + patronymic (-sunu / -ing); the noble houses carry an -ingas lineage-name; deed/animal bynames for the renowned; the Brittonic commons keep ap- / map- patronymics and the tud. Order given-first.
people_name_convention.dual_register: the Anglo-Saxon ruling stock keep OE dithematic names (Aethel-, Os-, Ead-, -wald, -here, -ric); the Romano-Brittonic commons keep Brythonic names (the Cad-, Cyn-, Mael-, Owain stems with ap- patronymics).
people_name_convention.theophoric: OE devotional names on the morphed stems (the Os- 'god-' element, Aelf- 'numinous-'): Os-here (god's-army), Aelf-red (counsel of the numinous); the Brittonic substrate keeps Mael- (devotee) and Gwas- (servant): Mael-Toran, Gwas-Gaian.

religion._note: Deity-names are morphs of the Agrippan canon - Anglo-Saxon reflexes PRIMARY (from family_germanic theonym_ancestors, the anglo_saxon column), Brythonic variants SECONDARY (reflexed from family_celtic theonym_set into p-Celtic), never real Germanic/Celtic gods. ALIGNMENT LENS IS PROVISIONAL: Arthurian Bryten reads Lawful (Aetern the Wyrd-father and the sworn fellowship of the Round Board), but an older Anglo-Saxon heathen layer reads Neutral (the ielde and the hus-wihta). Both treatments given below pending Jedidiah's alignment decision (see gdd-culture-emergence-and-territory.md open questions).
religion.the_one: Aetern (< Aeternus; Brythonic Eternan) - the Ancient One, the Wyrd-father above the lesser powers

sample_deity_renames.Tulrius: Thulor (Bryth. Toran) - the sun, the just brightness
sample_deity_renames.Realta: Realda (Bryth. Realtan) - the mother, the mercy-star

worship_by_alignment.Lawful: venerates the Lawful powers - Aetern foremost, Thulor the just-bright, Realda the merciful, Geand the steadfast earth - and names the Chaotic powers deoflu (devils), warded and unworshipped; the sworn fellowship and the just high-king are the social ideal
worship_by_alignment.Neutral: ancestral and local - the ielde (forebears and heroes), the hus-wihta (house-spirits), the powers of hearg-grove, holy well and hearth; the great gods invoked situationally rather than worshipped wholesale
worship_by_alignment.Chaotic: Venerates the Chaotic powers of the canon, and names the Lawful powers - and Aetern - as the tyrant-gods to be defied.

religion.demon_epithet_pattern: the Chaotic powers, warded as deoflu (devils) rather than worshipped, keep their morphs + an epithet: Maraxus -> Mearox the War-Brand (Bryth. Maragan); Vacidus -> Waecid the Unmaker (Bryth. Faicid); Lusanto -> Lusand the Hoard-Wyrm (Bryth. Losand).
religion.religious_orders_pattern: the Ealh (temple) or Hearg (grove-shrine) of [power]: 'the Ealh of Thulor', 'the Hearg of Geand'; the Brythonic substrate keeps Llan- (sacred enclosure): 'Llan-Toran'.
religion.saints_pattern: the ielde (ancestral heroes) and the hallowed dead of the cynn, honored at the beorg (barrow), the holy well (wielle) and the grove; the Brittonic seintiau (saints) honored at the Llan.

holy_symbol_motifs.Geand: the green hill beneath the standing stones (the Brittonic meini)
holy_symbol_motifs.Eorland: an iron sword crossed with a spear

banks_patterns.ships: the keel and the long-ship, named in OE kennings: 'the Grey Goose', 'the Wave-Stallion', 'Raven of the Weald'
banks_patterns.military_units: the [lineage] fyrd (levy) and the cyning's hearth-weru (hearth-troop / comitatus): 'the Fyrd of Bryten', 'the Ash-spears', 'the fellowship of the Round Board'
banks_patterns.taverns: 'The [Adjective] [Noun]': 'The White Hart', 'The Boar and Spear', 'The Green Knight'
banks_patterns.dungeons_ruins: fallen burhs, barrow-howes and the old Roman ceasters: 'the Burh of [name]', 'the Barrow of the Aethelings', 'the broken Caer'
